summary: Thomas Cleary (1949–2021) was a scholar in Buddhist studies, Sinology, and philosophy. He studied under E. Bruce Brooks and earned a Ph.D. from Harvard University and a JD from the University of California, Berkeley.

Thomas Craven (1844–1919) worked in linguistics and Indology. He earned an M.A. from Northwestern University (circa 1866–1870) and a B.D. from Garrett-Evangelical Theological Seminary (circa 1867–1871).

Thomas Doctor is a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar. He studied at Ka-Nying Shedrub Ling and the University of Lausanne, supervised by Tom Tillemans, Christian K. Wedemeyer, and several traditional masters. He holds a post at Rangjung Yeshe Institute.

Thomas E. Crow (born 1948) is an art historian who studied at Pomona College and UCLA. He directed the Getty Research Institute (2000–2007) and taught at several universities, including New York University as Rosalie Solow Professor of Modern Art (2007).

Thomas Edward Colebrooke (1813–1890) was an Indology and history scholar who studied at Eton College, East India Company College, and under Jagannatha. He served as President (1864–1882) and Vice-President (until 1890) of the Royal Asiatic Society.

Thomas Erskine Perry (1806–1882) worked in Indology and history. He studied at Charterhouse School, Trinity College, Cambridge, and the University of Munich. He served as a judge on Bombay's Supreme Court (1841–1852) and member of the Council of India (1859–1882).
Thomas Ethelbert Page (1850–1936) was a scholar of linguistics and history. He was educated at Shrewsbury School and St John's College, and later held a post at Charterhouse School from 1899 to 1936.

Thomas Freeman Yarnall is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology. He studied at the University of Washington and Columbia University under Robert A. F. Thurman and traditional teachers. At Columbia, he served as Executive Editor (attested 2007).

Thomas Fulton Cummings (1863–1942) was a linguist and Indologist educated at Union, Pittsburgh, and Westminster theological seminaries. He taught at Jhelum Theological Seminary, Biblical Seminary in New York, Union Theological Seminary, and Drew University.

Thomas George Percival Spear (1901–1982) was an Indologist and historian who earned his Ph.D. at St Catharine's College, Cambridge. He taught history at St. Stephen's College, Delhi, and served as Fellow, Bursar, and University Lecturer at Cambridge.

Thomas Grahame Bailey (1872–1942) was a linguistics and Indology scholar who earned a D.Litt. from the University of Edinburgh. From around 1920 to 1940, he served as Reader in Hindustani at SOAS University of London.

Thomas Henry Huxley (1825–1895) studied at Great Ealing School, University College London, and Charing Cross Hospital Medical School. He held an academic post at Imperial College London from circa 1854 to 1885.

Thomas Henry Thornton (1831–1913) was a historian and Indologist educated at St John's College, Oxford. He worked for the East India Company, was a Fellow of St John's and Calcutta University, and served as Vice-President of the University of the Punjab.

Thomas Holbein Hendley (1847–1917) worked in Indology and archaeology. He studied at St Bartholomew's Hospital, joined the Indian Medical Service in 1869, and served as a Fellow at the University of Calcutta from 1898 to 1903.

Thomas Howley (1831–1906) was a scholar in Indology and linguistics educated at Bishop Cowie's Grammar School. He served as Professor of Tamil, Telugu and Hindustani at King's College London and taught Telugu at the University of Oxford.

Thomas Hudson-Williams (1873–1961) was a linguist who studied at Bangor University, the University of London, and Greifswald under Heinrich Zimmer. He held posts at Bangor University from 1896, serving as Professor of Greek from 1904 to 1940.

Thomas J. Hopkins (1930–2021) worked in Indology and religious studies. Educated at MIT and Yale, he served as department chair at Franklin & Marshall College (1974–1994) and Director of Academic Affairs at the Oxford Centre for Hindu Studies (1998–1999).

Thomas James Mazanec specializes in Sinology and Buddhist studies. Educated at Calvin University, UC Boulder, and Princeton under Anna M. Shields and Stephen F. Teiser, he joined UC Santa Barbara, becoming Associate Professor (attested 2026).

Thomas Jülch (born 1975) is a Sinologist and Buddhist studies scholar. He studied at Goethe University Frankfurt, Hull, Heidelberg, and Munich (PhD). From 2013 to 2019, he was a postdoctoral researcher at Ghent University.
Thomas Lehmann is an Indologist and linguist who completed his doctoral studies under Ayyadurai Dhamotharan. He held an academic post at Heidelberg University (attested 2019).
